meta.subtitle: What was proposed, what the user decided, what shipped, and what's still open
meta.summary: Live decision log. Original proposal sections preserved with a status callout marking what the user decided and where each decision stands in implementation. Companion research (chart syntax landscape + visualization catalogue gap analysis) summarised at the top; full reports in notes/.

blocks.title: Where we are
blocks.summary: Five of six decisions answered, three shipped, two pending. Library adoption deferred. Research landed and recommends Vega-Lite as the syntactic baseline for the type-unification work.
bullets: **Shipped:** code → output label rename, function-grouped chart picker, smart-quiet table chrome (notebook feel — opacity 0.15 default, 1.0 on hover / focus / active state).

**Decided, not yet built:** chart-type unification — canonical types (`plot` / `arc` / `bar+mode`) with old type names kept as desugaring aliases that authors can still override per-property. Per the syntax research, the shape follows Vega-Lite's mark-composition pattern.

**Decided, not actionable yet:** no new chart libraries this round. Current SVG renderer stays. Library swaps revisited only after unification (we'll know the canonical shapes we'd want a library to render).
**Newly raised by the user:** runtime chart-type toggle — when data shape allows, let the reader flip between line / area / bar from the chart itself. Separate from unification but enabled by it.

**Research landed:** notes/chart-syntax-research.md (8 libraries surveyed, Vega-Lite recommended), notes/viz-catalog.md (1022 lines, eight sections — six-URL marketing-catalogue gap analysis + datavizcatalogue function taxonomy + D3 gallery + datavizproject.com). 15 visualization gaps and ~50 mode-variations on existing types identified.

blocks.title: Recently shipped
blocks.lead: What landed since the original review.

blocks.content: example-pair right column reads **Output**. Schema field renamed `render` → `output` (no backward-compat). 73 occurrences across 4 doc files migrated atomically. CSS class `.example-render` → `.example-output`.

29 chart cards across 8 function groups with single-word labels (per user feedback): **Compare**, **Trend**, **Distribution**, **Composition**, **Relationship**, **Hierarchy**, **Flow**, **Location**. Anchor ids match (`chart-fn-compare` etc.).

cards.title: Index page — code-output pairs for MD/JSON

blocks.content: The 'What a page looks like' section on the index page now shows each JSON / Markdown sample as an example pair — source on the left, the actual rendered block on the right. Five pairs total (callout, kpi-grid, blockquote→callout, inline-formatted list, mermaid diagram).

cards.title: Reference — markdown-conversion redesigned as a table

blocks.content: The 'Markdown → page kinds' compare-grid card (one 15-item bulleted list crammed into a single card) replaced with a two-column table (Markdown / Becomes). Tables sort, filter, and give the reader two scan axes. The card framing added noise without value.

Gear button on every chart's toolbar opens a floating popover anchored near the chart. Type dropdown populated by data-shape derivation (no per-chart `compatible_with` field). Live re-render on every change via host swap — the chart visibly transforms in place. Mode chips, marks chips, and an arc-end input round out the popover for the unified families.

Same gear pattern on every table. Click → floating popover holding the view toggle and group-by select (moved out of the toolbar at open, returned at close — same DOM, same listeners). Toolbar at rest is now two affordances: filter + gear.

Filter-columns section in the table popover: one input per header. Combines with the global text filter and chip-rack via AND. Verified: typing in one column input narrows 16 rows → 4; clear restores all.

cards.title: T3 — multi-column sort with rank badge

blocks.content: Click cycles primary sort; shift-click adds a secondary, then tertiary, etc. The arrow indicator stays; a small accent-coloured rank badge appears only when more than one column is active so single-column tables stay quiet.

From the catalogue-research top-8: **dot-plot · density · candlestick · sunburst · marimekko · stream · violin · beeswarm**. Each has a doc section + an example pair + a card in the appropriate function group. Chart-type count rises from 29 to 37.

Plot family accepts the canonical Vega-Lite-style input: `data: [...records]` + `encoding: { x, y, color, size, label }` + `marks: [...]`. Legacy `series` shape keeps working. The desugar runs at the renderer entry; downstream code is untouched. Same pattern is the template for arc / bar / categorical / flow in upcoming rounds.

cards.title: Q1 — toolbar bugs fixed (gear svg + button order + bar previews)

blocks.content: Gear svg in tables was rendering 0×0; sized to 14×14. Toolbar order normalised across charts + tables + diagrams: data-output actions on the left, separator, then chart-side affordances (Configure · Expand). Bar / stacked-bar / grouped-bar / bullet previews inside the picker cards were invisible (160px label column collapsed the 1fr track to 0); switched the grid to `minmax(40px, max-content) minmax(0, 1fr) auto`.

A temporary `.okt-theme-swapping` class on `<html>` silences every transition for the two frames around the data-theme flip. The page repaints in one pass instead of every transition animating independently.

cards.title: Q4 — docs reorg (Tables → Charts → Diagrams; scatter heading split; new viz categorised)

blocks.content: Index step-flow reorders to Reference · Tables · Charts · Diagrams. The chart-scatter-line heading split into its own `type: scatter` section. The 8 new chart sections (dot-plot, density, candlestick, sunburst, marimekko, stream, violin, beeswarm) move from the intro into family-categorical / family-distribution / family-trend / family-partwhole.

Tooltips remain `position: fixed` (so they sit above the lightbox) but now track their anchor's getBoundingClientRect on scroll / resize. The reader can open a tooltip, scroll, and the tooltip slides along with the chart. requestAnimationFrame coalesces multiple scroll events into one paint.

Hovering or focusing a legend entry fades every other series / slice / segment / radar-area to opacity 0.18; the matching shape stays at 1 with an accent drop-shadow. Works on Cartesian and non-Cartesian charts. Released on mouseleave / blur.
Hover on a mermaid node now triggers an accent drop-shadow + accent stroke. Click handlers are native to mermaid via `click NodeId "url"`. Pan/zoom is the same shared lightbox stage.

Any label that could obscure data tags itself with `.okc-label-overlay`. CSS `:has()` rule fades it to 0.15 when any data point is hovered, a tooltip is visible, or a slice/dot is click-pinned. Applied to quadrant corner labels today; same class is the convention for any future overlay label.

cards.title: Q7 — vertical cursor on every chart type

blocks.content: Generic `_wireGenericVerticalCursor` SVG helper wired into histogram, box-plot, candlestick, density, beeswarm, dot-plot. DIV-based bar / stacked-bar / grouped-bar get the same affordance via an absolute-positioned dashed line that follows the pointer's x. Cartesian / ridgeline / sparkline already had it. Standard everywhere now.

`orientation: horizontal | vertical` property in the chart schema. Bar family implemented today via a `.bar-chart-vertical` CSS class + a shared `--bar-pct` CSS var on the fills. Single / stacked / grouped all flip cleanly. Violin / box-plot / histogram / candlestick orientation switch needs an SVG-axis-swap per renderer — follow-up.

cards.title: B2 — system bug review + fixes (kit.json 404, missing cursors)

blocks.content: Playwright sweep across all 37 chart types + tables + index page. Two real bugs found: kit.json 404 (file lived at docs/kit.json but build expected ./kit.json; moved to project root) and missing vertical cursor on violin + stream. Both fixed. Everything else checked clean — 37/37 charts render, all toolbars order correctly, tables popover works end-to-end, dark-mode colors all theme-correct, console clean.

cards.title: B3 — round-2 audit: kit.json placement + slope label clipping + favicon noise

blocks.content: Second Playwright pass at 1440×900 + 360×800 across all 43 chart types and every doc page. Three real defects found and fixed:

items: **kit.json belongs next to docs/, not the project root.** B2's quick fix unblocked the build but broke `oku serve` against the source tree (chrome.js resolves from __okuDocsRoot = /docs/, so /docs/kit.json must exist). Moved back to docs/kit.json (which the schema's own description prescribes); added a `find_kit_json(root)` helper that probes docs/ first, falls back to root. Both dev and dist now work.

**Slope chart's right-side endpoint labels clipped past the SVG edge** because pad.right=80 was too narrow for typical `value · label` readouts. Made pad.right scale to the longest label (24 + 6·chars, min 80). Title row also overlapped the BEFORE/AFTER column heads — bumped pad.top from 44 to 56 so column heads land at y≥44 (22-unit gap).
**Favicon 404 on every page load** — synthesized a 0-byte image/png response so the dev server stops logging the error without polluting the source tree with a real binary.

blocks.content: Verified numerically: 0 SVG text labels overflow the slope chart's svg bounds (was 3), /docs/kit.json: 304 (was 404), /favicon.ico: 200 (was 404), charts.html console: 0 errors (was 1).

cards.title: Q10 deeper — mermaid flowchart neighbor highlight

blocks.content: Hovering a node now lights up its incident edges + neighbor nodes while the rest of the graph dims to 0.25 opacity. Reading a multi-step flow becomes path-tracing instead of visual-search.

Wiring leans on conventions Mermaid v10 already emits for flowcharts: nodes carry `data-id="<NodeId>"`; edges carry `LS-<source>` + `LE-<target>` classes. `_wireNeighborHighlight` walks the SVG once per render, builds an adjacency map, and binds mouseenter/leave + focus/blur on every node. Nodes also get tabindex=0 so keyboard users can step through. Verified: hovering JSON in the index-page flowchart stamps data-okd-active on JSON (self) + JSON→RJ edge + RJ neighbor (3 elements). svg[data-okd-has-active]="1" present during hover, removed on leave.

Fallback shape: diagram types without `data-id` on nodes (sequence, gantt, journey, state, mindmap) get no extra wiring — the loop early-exits when nodes.length === 0. The pre-existing single-node hover-lift rule remains.

**waterfall · lollipop · dumbbell · polar-area · gantt · bump**. Each ships renderer + schema + doc section + picker card + vertical cursor (where it makes sense). Chart-type count: 37 → 43. Catalog gap items: 1, 2 (dot-plot variant), 3 (dumbbell), 10 (polar-area), 12 (gantt), 9 (bump).

Table controls at opacity 0.15 by default. Reveal on hover or keyboard focus. Force-show via `:has()` when filter has text, any chip is active, or view is non-default. Charts and code blocks were already hover-only.

Canonical types: `plot` (with `marks: [dots|line|area]`), `arc` (with `mode: pie|donut` + `arc: {start, end}` + `inner_radius`), `bar` (with `mode: single|stacked|grouped`). Legacy names (scatter / line / area / pie / donut / stacked-bar / grouped-bar) keep working as aliases that desugar to the canonical form with appropriate defaults — and author overrides win over alias presets. Verified: all 6 canonical+alias Cartesian forms produce matching DOM, donut+pie+arc-override all render correctly, all 29 existing chart types still pass regression tests.

blocks.title: Research findings (this session)
blocks.lead: Two reports landed; both inform the pending work.

blocks.content: Full report: `notes/chart-syntax-research.md`. Surveyed eight libraries — Vega-Lite, Observable Plot, D3, ECharts, Plotly, Highcharts, Chart.js, Apache Superset. The recommendation is **Vega-Lite as the syntactic baseline** for our unification: its `mark: [...]` composition pattern is the closest analogue to `type: plot, marks: [...]`, and its encoding model handles cross-shape rendering (same data, different mark) cleanly.

blocks.title: What we should take from Vega-Lite
blocks.content: The mark-composition model and the principle that 'a chart is data + encoding + mark', not 'a chart is a top-level type'. The reader writes the data once and switches marks to switch chart shapes — that maps directly to the user's runtime-toggle idea (decision 6).

blocks.title: What we should NOT take
blocks.content: Vega-Lite's depth — selection signals, layered transforms, complex `encoding.color.condition` blocks. These shrink AI emission's success rate. Keep the surface flat: data + marks + a small property bag per mark.

Full report: `notes/viz-catalog.md` (1022 lines, eight sections). Cross-references oku's 29 chart types against six marketing catalogues + the D3 gallery + datavizcatalogue's function taxonomy + datavizproject.com's ~150-type reference.

rows: Master list + 15 gaps + 10 improvements to existing types. Highlights pictograms, marimekko, density plot, candlestick, sunburst, stream graph, violin, dot plot, error-bar.
Eight function categories that drove the new picker grouping. Recommends hybrid (function primary, family secondary) — shipped in B.
20 new candidates (beeswarm, contour, sunburst, sankey-with-cycles, etc.) + 15 interactivity techniques worth lifting (zoom-to-region, brush-to-filter, lasso-select, force-relax, click-to-fix-node).

10 distinct new candidates + 51 named variations of existing oku types that could become `mode:` switches post-unification (radial-bar, 100%-stacked, marimekko-as-stacked-bar-with-scaled-widths, etc.).

blocks.title: Top-priority new visualizations (synthesised across all four sources)
blocks.content: **Sunburst** (hierarchy alternative to treemap), **Violin** (distribution alternative to box-plot), **Marimekko** (variable-width stacked bar — earns a `mode` on bar), **Density plot / KDE** (smoothed histogram), **Candlestick** (financial OHLC, distinct shape), **Stream graph** (alternative stacked area), **Dot plot** (one-axis comparison), **Beeswarm** (jittered scatter for one-axis distribution). Eight items — discuss before adding.

blocks.title: The north star
blocks.lead: Restate the contract so every later decision is measured against it. (Unchanged from the original review.)

blocks.title: Contract (from the user, paraphrased)
blocks.content: JSON is the substrate so AI can read / write / modify content without fighting style or glue markup. The presentation should be capable yet simple — simplicity is the ultimate sophistication. Pre-defined structures should be enough for the 90% case, but raw HTML/JS escape hatches should remain available for the 10%.

Two failure modes to guard against. **Drift toward complexity:** every new feature adds schema surface, runtime branches, and visual-language vocabulary the reader has to learn. Each addition is locally justifiable; collectively they erode the contract. **Drift toward purity:** rejecting every addition leaves the reader with bullet-points and tables for everything a chart could illustrate. Equally a failure.

The discipline: every new primitive must answer two questions. **(1) Can AI emit this in one obvious shape, with no per-page judgement calls?** (2) Does the rendered result earn the schema cost — i.e., does the reader recognise the shape faster than they'd parse a paragraph + bullets?

blocks.title: Unify the bar family
blocks.lead: Three chart types today differ only in how multi-series rows render. Collapse to one with a mode switch.

blocks.title: Decision: Yes — alias desugar (Status: shipped)
blocks.content: `type: bar` is canonical with `mode: single | stacked | grouped`. `stacked-bar` / `grouped-bar` keep working as aliases that desugar to `bar, mode: stacked|grouped`. Author can override any preset on the alias form. No backward-compat break — all existing pages pass regression tests.

AI picks one shape (`type: bar`) and answers one question (`mode`). Single-series omits `mode` (defaults to `single`); both series-modes share the same `categories` + `series` shape. Post-unification, the bar `mode` enum can widen to absorb research-recommended variants (marimekko = variable-width stacked, percent-stacked, radial-bar).

blocks.title: Unify scatter / line / area
blocks.lead: Same axes, same data shape, different mark.

blocks.title: Decision: Yes — alias desugar (Status: shipped)
blocks.content: `type: plot` is canonical with `marks: [dots | line | area]`. `scatter` / `line` / `area` keep working as aliases. Author can override marks on either form. Mark-composition matches Vega-Lite. Verified: all 6 canonical+alias Cartesian forms produce identical dots/lines/areas counts.

blocks.title: Enabler for decision 6 (runtime type-toggle)
blocks.content: Once data + axes are decoupled from mark choice, the chart can offer the reader an inline picker: switch the SAME chart between dots / line / area / bar at runtime by mutating `marks` and re-rendering. The data shape doesn't change, the encoding does. This is the Vega-Lite pattern.

blocks.title: Unify donut / pie / gauge
blocks.lead: Three primitives that share an arc-geometry renderer.

blocks.title: Decision: Yes for pie+donut, no for gauge (Status: shipped)
blocks.content: `type: arc` is canonical for pie + donut. `pie` and `donut` stay as aliases, with `arc: { start, end }` and `inner_radius` overridable on either. Verified: `type: pie + arc.end=270` produces a 3/4 pie; `type: donut + inner_radius=0.3` produces a thicker ring. Gauge stays its own type — different data shape (value + zones).

blocks.title: Future addition (post-unification)
blocks.content: **Sunburst** — a multi-level radial hierarchy chart — fits naturally as `type: arc, levels: [...]` where each level adds an outer ring. Surfaced by the visualization-catalogue research as a top-priority gap. Implement once the arc renderer is unified.

blocks.title: Interaction budget — smart hiding, no settings
blocks.lead: Capable yet quiet — notebook feel. No new toggle.

blocks.title: Decision: smart defaults, no setting (Status: partial — table chrome shipped, more surfaces pending)
blocks.content: User explicitly rejected an `interaction_density` switch. Default behaviour should cover both worlds — surfaces stay quiet until the reader intends to use them (hover / focus / non-default state). The system should feel like a well-designed notebook: present but not distracting.

opacity 0.15 default; 1.0 on hover/focus; force-show via `:has()` when filter has text or any chip active or view non-default.

Earlier polish locked it as a flush corner label. A regression test forbids hover state. Future trim: only render when the block sits inside a multi-language sequence — needs chrome.js detection, not pure CSS.
Fold detection skipped on blocks under 8 lines. Short blocks no longer add gutter chevrons — a 3-line shell command stays clean.

Drag handle resting state is a 2px bar in `--border-soft`; widens to 20px on hover and brightens to `--accent-strong`. Reviewed in this round and judged already at the right level — further fade would make it undiscoverable.

blocks.title: Is our chart declaration syntax the best?
blocks.lead: User question (paraphrased): break the system into building blocks; think in units; does the current chart declaration syntax represent the task well? Honest answer below.

blocks.title: Honest answer: no, not yet. Today's syntax is type-first; the right shape is data + encoding + mark.
blocks.content: We've collapsed three families to canonical types (plot, arc, bar). The other ~22 types still 'own' their data shape — each renderer expects a custom payload (`slices`, `cells`, `tree`, `nodes+links`, `regions`, ...). That's the drift the unification was meant to reverse, and we only finished part of the job.
Strip every chart down to its atoms and three repeating ideas fall out — true for every chart we render, true for every chart in the catalogue research.

rows: A table of records. Same shape every time: array of objects with author-named fields.
Which field of each record drives which visual channel — x, y, color, size, angle, radius, source, target, value, ...
The geometric shape drawn for each record — dot, line, area, bar, arc, tile, rect, link, path, ...

blocks.title: What that looks like in JSON
blocks.content: Today's `type: "scatter"` becomes `data + encoding: { x: "col", y: "col" } + mark: "dot"`. Today's `type: "heatmap"` becomes the same `data`, `encoding: { x: "row", y: "col", color: "value" }`, `mark: "tile"`. Today's `type: "sankey"` becomes `data` (the link table), `encoding: { source: "from", target: "to", value: "qty" }`, `mark: "flow"`. The author writes one data shape and decides how columns map to channels. The renderer reads encoding + mark and draws.

blocks.title: Why this is better than what we have

items: Each of 29 types has a bespoke payload shape — the AI has to remember 29 schemas.
Switching chart type often means rewriting the data structure (`series` → `slices` → `cells` → `nodes+links`).
Same data → different chart requires copy-paste and re-shaping. The data-shape-derived type switch we just decided to build has to handle every shape's permutation.
Catalogue gaps (sunburst, violin, marimekko, ...) each add another bespoke payload.
One universal data shape. The AI emits a record array — same skill every time.
Switching chart type is one field edit: `mark: "line"` → `mark: "bar"`. No data reshaping.
Compatibility falls out for free: any chart whose marks consume the current encoding is compatible.
New chart types add a mark grammar entry; the data + encoding shape doesn't change. Sunburst / violin / marimekko stop being big additions.

blocks.title: But — what makes oku oku is on the line
blocks.content: Vega-Lite went all the way to this model. Its schema is ~500 pages of options, conditions, layered transforms — perfect for analysts, brutal for AI authors who 'just want a bar chart'. Our advantage today is that `type: "bar"` JUST WORKS without thinking about encodings. Lose that and we lose the AI-friendliness that's the whole point of the kit.

blocks.title: Proposed direction: dual-form, not replacement
blocks.content: Keep `type: "bar"` / `type: "line"` / `type: "pie"` etc. as the AI-friendly entry point. ALSO accept the canonical `mark + encoding + data` form for power users and runtime mutation. The alias-desugar pattern we just shipped becomes the convention for the whole kit — type aliases desugar to canonical mark+encoding internally. AI emits `type: "bar"`; the runtime translates; the popup mutates the canonical form when the reader switches mark. Two surfaces, one engine.

rows: Build the live-config popup (decision 6) with data-shape-derived type list
**Next** — it's a smaller proof-of-concept of the mark + encoding model. The popup needs to mutate the chart's mark independently of data, which forces us to internally separate the two.
Refactor the renderer to a single mark + encoding pipeline
**After the popup proves the idea.** Migrate one family at a time (plot already half-there → bar → arc → categorical (heatmap/waffle/treemap) → flow (sankey/chord/network) → spec (geo, gauge)).
Drop `compatible_with` proposal entirely (the user already vetoed it)
Done — derivation lives in code, not in the schema.

blocks.title: Open question for you
blocks.content: Greenlight the dual-form refactor? It's the right call long-term but it's a multi-session investment with one breakage risk (a poorly-tested mark migration could regress existing pages). I'd run it as: popup first → one family-at-a-time refactor → tests guard every step. Or — defer the refactor, ship just the popup with the current type-first model. Your call.

blocks.title: Live chart configuration (decision 6 — confirmed direction)
blocks.lead: User direction: hide the type-switch behind a gear button on the chart toolbar; click → live configuration popup positioned near the chart. Type is one configurable knob; mode, marks, arc overrides, etc. live in the same popup so the reader can experiment with the whole rendering live.

blocks.title: Decision: button → popup, derive compatible types from data shape (no `compatible_with` field needed)
blocks.content: Quote: "we shouldn't bother with adding compatible types to every single chart. We already know which chart types are compatible with each other based on the data shape, or to be more accurate: we know which chart types could be used to represent a certain data shape only by looking into the data shape."

**Mostly yes, with one edge case.** Compatibility falls out of data shape for the great majority of types — same shape means the renderer has everything it needs to draw any chart that consumes that shape. A few shapes admit a semantic ambiguity (a sequence of `{x, y}` could be a continuous trend or a categorical comparison — that's an author judgement, not a data fact), but the runtime can offer both options and let the reader pick. We don't need to pre-declare anything.

rows: scatter · line · area · plot (with any marks combo); bar (if author treats x as categorical)
bubble · scatter (size becomes a decorative dimension)
bar · stacked-bar · grouped-bar; line / area (treating category index as x)
pie · donut · waffle · arc (with any mode); horizontal bar (one bar per slice)
gauge · bullet · sparkline-as-trend (if a value history is attached)
histogram · bar (bin index as category); area (smoothed)
heatmap · calendar-heatmap (if row/col are date axes)

blocks.title: Implementation
blocks.content: A single `getCompatibleTypes(block)` function in the renderer inspects the data shape and returns the list of types that consume it. The config popup calls that function to populate its type-switch dropdown. No `compatible_with` field on individual charts — the rule lives in code once.

items: **Gear icon** in the chart toolbar (alongside copy / download / expand). Hover-only like the other toolbar buttons.
**Click → floating popover**, anchored near the chart's top-right corner with viewport-clamp (same logic the tooltip uses).
**Popup content:** Type dropdown (populated by `getCompatibleTypes`) · mode/marks chips · arc overrides (when applicable) · inner_radius slider · close button.
**Live re-render:** every popup change mutates the chart's attributes and re-runs `_render()` in place. No reload.
**Dismiss:** click outside, Esc, or the popup's own × button.
**Smart-hide:** popup itself is opaque; the gear button follows the same hover-reveal as the rest of the toolbar.

blocks.title: Library adoption
blocks.lead: Honest cost / benefit per candidate. The earlier review's recommendation stands — no new libraries this round.

blocks.title: Decision: defer all (Status: decided)
blocks.content: Library adoption pays off once we know the unified shapes — then we can ask 'does library X render this shape better than our renderer?' instead of asking 'should we use X?' in the abstract. Until then, the existing SVG renderer wins on control + predictability + zero bundle weight.

rows: **Defer.** Imposes its own data-binding model. Less code per chart, more cognitive shift per chart.
**Watch.** Mark-composition aligns with our unification but it owns SVG output → we'd lose hover/pin/cursor control.
**Watch — syntactic inspiration, not runtime.** Take the schema shape (mark composition), not the runtime.
**Keep.** Each earns its weight on a distinct problem (diagrams / highlighting / search).

blocks.content: example-pair right column reads **Output** (was 'Render'); left column reads **Code** (was 'Source'). The schema fields stay `code` and `render` for backwards-compat — only the visible labels changed.

blocks.lead: What could go wrong with the pending work.

rows: Existing pages emit `scatter` / `line` / `area` / `stacked-bar` / `grouped-bar` / `pie` / `donut`. If aliases break, all 18 doc pages fail to render.

Aliases are non-negotiable, not optional. Test matrix: every old type name must produce the same DOM as before. Schema accepts both old and new; renderer normalises. Tests: existing chart-content regression tests already cover this surface.
Reader switches to a mark the data doesn't actually support (e.g. line on categorical x).
`compatible_with` is author-declared, not auto-inferred. Author opts in only when they've checked the data shape. UI hides the toggle when only one option exists.
Hidden chrome makes affordances undiscoverable — first-time visitors don't know there's a filter input on the table.
Default opacity is 0.15, not 0. Affordance is visible but quiet — a hint, not a hide. Force-show on active state means the user never loses sight of state they've already set.
Each new chart type expands the schema and the runtime. Adding all 15 from the gap list would re-introduce the drift the north star guards against.

Add one at a time, each with a written justification against the two north-star questions. Sunburst is high-value (different hierarchy view); pictograms are low-value (a styling variant of waffle). Discriminate.
